text:
leo: FYI customer-facing incident: after last night's IdP JWK rotation some sign-ins fail with 'unknown kid' and our SCIM provisioning jobs are creating accounts without org roles. KMS shows AccessDenied on Decrypt for a wrapped attribute used to provision role mappings (we store role blobs encrypted at rest).

leo: Error from auth-service logs: "verify_jwt: kid not found in cached jwks; fetching jwks failed: 403 Forbidden" then later "provisioner: decrypt error: AccessDeniedException" 

nisha: Two parallel issues could be happening: 1) IdP rotated JWKs and the jwks_uri is returning 403 from their CDN (so our cached JWK is stale -> kid mismatch). 2) our KMS key policy may have been tightened during last week's security hardening so the service principal that runs provisioning lost decrypt rights. Both would cause fallback behavior in provisioning.

dan: I pulled the IdP jwks_uri manually and got 403 for the org-specific JWK URL, but the global jwks endpoint works. Looks like the IdP rolled out a scoped ACL change. I'm opening a ticket with their SRE to re-open the org jwks endpoint.

dan: Meanwhile, the KMS CloudTrail shows `Decrypt` calls from `arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/redwood-provisioner/instance` returning `AccessDenied`. The key policy was changed at 2026-05-01T03:12Z.

leo: Ouch. We have two simultaneous failures: token verification fails (kid not found) so the user attributes fallback to email-only; provisioning tries to read encrypted mapping but KMS denies -> roles empty -> default to minimal viewer. Explains customer reports.

nisha: Short-term mitigation: (A) add a JWK fetch fallback to use the global jwks URI if org-scoped returns 403 (implement safe retry/backoff), (B) add provisioning audit rule: if roles missing, mark job failed and backoff instead of creating with default viewer.

security-bot: alert: keypolicy-change detected on alias/ci-redwood-provisioner at 2026-05-01T03:12:17Z by admin@security. Suggested action: review recent key policy PR #4123.

dan: I reverted the key policy to allow decrypt for the provisioner role, and requested a scoped policy that explicitly lists the role ARNs via PR. deploy-bot: key-policy rollback applied to alias/ci-redwood-provisioner.

deploy-bot: deploy started: service/provisioner v3.9.2 -> v3.9.3 (jwks fallback + provisioning guard). CI: green.

leo: After the key policy revert I re-ran a few provisioning runs against the affected orgs: KMS decrypts now succeed and roles are assigned correctly. IdP SRE acknowledged the jwks ACL rollout and will restore org jwks; they will add a 24h grace window on future rotations.

nisha: Follow-ups: 1) add healthcheck metric `jwks_fetch_failures` and alert if >5 in 5m, 2) implement JWK cache TTL + background refresh and a fallback to global jwks, 3) add CloudTrail monitor for Decrypt AccessDenied spikes, 4) change provisioning to fail-fast on missing roles and expose an audit event so customer-facing teams can triage.

leo: Root cause summary for postmortem: simultaneous external IdP jwk ACL change (caused kid lookup failures) + internal key policy tightening (caused KMS AccessDenied) produced a chaining failure: JWTs couldn't be validated -> provisioning tried to act with partial attributes -> KMS prevented reading encrypted role mappings -> silent fallback produced incorrect RBAC. Remediation applied and follow-ups assigned.

nisha: I'll draft the postmortem and customer notification for the affected orgs. Also adding an action to run a combined smoke test (jwks fetch + KMS decrypt + full provisioning flow) during any future key or jwks rotations.

leo: Thanks all — looks stable now. Closing incident channel and will move notes to the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
